synthesis.paragraph: Four of today's papers carry the tag "Urban Transport and Accessibility," which cover how built environment factors shape demand-responsive transport in Germany, a validation framework for longitudinal cycling-infrastructure change in OpenStreetMap, the effects of activity-travel chaining on peak and off-peak travel, and factors influencing bike-sharing travel behavior in Beijing. Three of these papers are also tagged under "Transportation and Mobility Innovations," namely the studies on demand-responsive transport in Germany, activity-travel chaining, and Beijing bike-sharing behavior. Outside of these groups, one paper analyzes the political theology of state-led gentrification and heritagization around the Yogyakarta Kraton in Indonesia. Another study examines the usability perceptions and willingness of older adults in Mississippi to adopt microtransit. Finally, a third paper analyzes how global container shipping networks shape domestic port hinterlands in Japan.
